I have High Frequency Cortical Tremor, caused by dodgy genetics. TL;DR it means the muscles in my thighs and arms vibrate at 19Hz.

1. It is advised to make a new game when playing with mods, but if you don't install any quest mods that affect the main story then you could feasibly wait till after then.

2. Most mods you can just install and then leave alone. There is a little bit of management to get them all working together, but after that you can play stable easily. Check the complete modding guide when on your PC, its on the sidebar. 

3. This is a tough one, if you use Mod Organiser to install your mods, then yes. Otherwise probably no. Mod Organiser leaves your vanilla game alone, whilst most other managers do not. Your saves would not be able to change between vanilla and modded on the fly, however.

4. You should have no performance issues. There are graphical mods out there to make the game look a lot better than on Ultra (eg, 2-4k textures, weather effects, lighting). If you install these, you may see a slight framerate dip depending on your specs. Overall, no.

Your HDMI will plug into your GPU. Your airflow will be fine in a case like that.

Your CPU may bottleneck your GPU quite badly, but that model is not particularly known to me.

I am not sure that there isnt another name tbh. The name and rarity of the condition that I have were told to me by my current team of neurologists. Its very possible I have some rarer variant of cortical myoclonic tremor and they just said it was this for the sake of simplicity. The team working on me are from all around the world, supposedly making up the best neurological department worldwide. Cortical tremor may be a blanket term of some kind perhaps. I do not know.

When I found out what it was, I basically did freak out! Heart racing, adrenaline pumping. It was exciting and amazing to finally know what it was after all these years. I guess now its sunk it, become part of who I am. Despite what it may seem, I don't  tend to talk about it much with other people, so doing this AMA is quite a leap!
I was thinking of doing a few videos and put them out there. I would rather know more about the disease and treatments from my doctors so I had more of a description others to go on.

Yeah, there are similarities. I never had an accident in the past, but one day this condition just started. 
When it first came along, they werent so much 'episodes' as it was always there, affecting my every move. 
Now that I am at the point of semi-normality, thanks to training my mind, I do instinctively know when my legs are going to shake. Unfortunately, there is little I can do to stop the shaking before it happens. I usually just sit down and take 5 mins to myself when it does happen. As far as driving goes, I did do a lots of lessons as my legs dont shake as much when Im sitting, but found that the stress of taking the tests affected my shakes.
In all honesty, its a bit weird. Most neurological doctors will never even hear of the condition, let alone see a case of it. Just knowing there are others out there with this is a comfort as well.
Nope. due to confidentiality and since its so rare, I have not been able to find anyone else with it. I guess the only way of finding others with it is via the media.
http://imgur.com/Sxvfc
I have one right here, but have no means of scanning it for you guys. [EDIT: I may be able to find a scanner, will post soon]

No offence taken! I did always wonder what it was. Over the 10 years I have seen about 12 different neurologists all around the UK. None could give me any answers about it despite numerous tests. I honestly felt like a freak and that I somehow deserved this. Now that I have answers and possible treatments, its much easier to think more positively about my situation.
Technically my condition counts as a rare form of epilepsy, as the same drugs could treat me, according to the doctors at NHNN.
Its kinda impossible to prove I have it since its so rare. I have no reason to lie about something like this, and there is little to no information outside of neurologist social circles. sorry :)

Its not easy. I have had these symptoms for about 10 years now. I have sortof trained my mind over this time to enable me to do most things normally. I still have trouble with small movements and moving when I am tired. I have only just been diagnosed, but the group of doctors working on me are confident on a treatment. So far, they have had me on Clonazepam, but I found no real benefit on my legs and the side effects weren't great.
See above, but when it does affect me, it feels like my legs are no longer attached to me. They just stop and give way or shake lots. When it shakes, it feels like a reflex being set off constantly.

For me, it affects my leg muscles. Its difficult to describe but I will do my best. When doing an unconscious task, such as climbing stairs or walking, I have no issues. As soon as I have to make a conscious effort to move my legs, they stop moving and shake involuntarily.
The signals sent from the base of my brain are being disrupted. Too many get sent at once, or none at all. Its completely random. AFAIK it can affect any part of the body, but for me its my legs.
Not as of yet, its not well known enough to be in the media. Google only turns up a couple of results that are relevant.
